liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (1 review): Shakedown Street is described as fantastic and funkadelic [22]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The China Cat into Rider jam runs at hyperdrive pace, with furious rhythm playing from Weir [20]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Reviewer names Looks Like Rain as a highlight, though the first set overall left them unmoved [21]
- **Space** (1 other source): A 0:44 patch in Space comes from a Sennheiser 441 blend source; Other One space is within The Other One track [4]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Bob's slashing, atonal rhythm playing stands out in The Other One [28]
- **One More Saturday Night** (1 review): Saturday Night and Touch of Grey carry kinetic energy that gets the reviewer dancing [26]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-07-21.112806.beyer-senn.daweez.d5scott.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 22 songs; 149 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1984-07-21.sonyecm.unknown.gale.88940.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 155 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd1984-07-21.166981.senn441.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 148 min [4]
- **gd1984-07-21.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.96410.flac24**: soundboard; 20 songs; 147 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [8]. Said about its sound: The cassette master supplies changes in mix and levels during Shakedown Street [8]
- **gd84-07-21.sbd.cole.14329.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 141 min; rated 4.4/5 by 15 [9]. Said about its sound: Drums is cut short on this tape, omitting Mickey's balaphone section; Phil's bass level fluctuates in the mix, especially during Shakedown Street, swinging abruptly between booming and nearly absent; Heavy echo on Jerry's and Bob's mics at times hurts the recording; Eyes of the World sounds tunnel-like [20][21][25]
- **gd1984-07-21.sbd.lai.1616.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 141 min [12]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended and ranks this two-day run, with 7/22, among their top ten of roughly 500 shows [24]
- An 18-year-old attendee could walk close to the stage front and see Jerry up close without crowding [27]
- Jerry looked in rough shape to the reviewer, who later saw about 100 more shows [27]
- The venue was a rodeo arena a few hundred yards from the Pacific, band facing the sea, with beach camping all weekend [28]
- This show is overshadowed by the better circulated 7/22 show, though the reviewer finds it a barnburner throughout [20]
- Recommended as a companion to the preceding Berkeley shows; reviewer also points to the 1984 Merriweather Althea [22]
- Reviewer calls the post-Drums segment among the best they have heard [26]
- Reviewer calls these the best Ventura shows the band played, and notes a rare mid-first-set China>Rider [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-07-21.112806.beyer-senn.daweez.d5scott.flac16**: taped by Da Weez; transferred by D5scott; source: Source: 2 Beyer M160 & 1 Sennheiser 421 Microphones (30 feet from stage-center) > Nak MX100 W/2001 > Sony TC-D5M - analog master cassettes; [1]
- **gd1984-07-21.sonyecm.unknown.gale.88940.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Dan Gale; transferred by Dan Gale; source: Sony ECM-939LT (dead center, halfway between sbd and the stage) > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D6C) [2]. Also: Patches come from a soundboard run through CASM and a Sony R500 into Samplitude, then FLAC; resampled from 48 to 44.1kHz [2]
- **gd1984-07-21.166981.senn441.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Jim Vita's 1st generation cassettes [4]
- **gd1984-07-21.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.96410.flac24**: taped by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R90) [8]
- **gd84-07-21.sbd.cole.14329.sbeok.shnf**: source: Cool Edit fix of previous shn set SBD Master Reel-> DAT->ZA2- >CD, by Matthew Cole [9]
- **gd1984-07-21.sbd.lai.1616.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Mike Lai; source: Master Reel->DAT->ZA2->CD [12]. Also: Reviewer disputes the listed reel lineage, suggesting a DAT copy of an MSC source or of the PCM [30]

claims.text: The China Cat into Rider jam runs at hyperdrive pace, with furious rhythm playing from Weir
This show is overshadowed by the better circulated 7/22 show, though the reviewer finds it a barnburner throughout
Drums is cut short on this tape, omitting Mickey's balaphone section
Phil's bass level fluctuates in the mix, especially during Shakedown Street, swinging abruptly between booming and nearly absent
Reviewer names Looks Like Rain as a highlight, though the first set overall left them unmoved
Shakedown Street is described as fantastic and funkadelic
Recommended as a companion to the preceding Berkeley shows; reviewer also points to the 1984 Merriweather Althea
Reviewer attended and ranks this two-day run, with 7/22, among their top ten of roughly 500 shows
Heavy echo on Jerry's and Bob's mics at times hurts the recording; Eyes of the World sounds tunnel-like
Saturday Night and Touch of Grey carry kinetic energy that gets the reviewer dancing
Reviewer calls the post-Drums segment among the best they have heard
An 18-year-old attendee could walk close to the stage front and see Jerry up close without crowding
Jerry looked in rough shape to the reviewer, who later saw about 100 more shows
The venue was a rodeo arena a few hundred yards from the Pacific, band facing the sea, with beach camping all weekend
Bob's slashing, atonal rhythm playing stands out in The Other One
Reviewer calls these the best Ventura shows the band played, and notes a rare mid-first-set China>Rider
Reviewer disputes the listed reel lineage, suggesting a DAT copy of an MSC source or of the PCM
Patches come from a soundboard run through CASM and a Sony R500 into Samplitude, then FLAC; resampled from 48 to 44.1kHz
Transferred by Charlie Miller from Jim Vita's first-generation cassettes
A 0:44 patch in Space comes from a Sennheiser 441 blend source; Other One space is within The Other One track
Source is a front-of-board Sony ECM-939LT cassette master, taped by Joani Walker, with Paul Scotton supplying the cassettes
The cassette master supplies changes in mix and levels during Shakedown Street
